History › Notable people

Notable people from 15068

Research compiled Sept. 23, 2026

21 people born, raised or remembered in the three cities, from the inventor of Kevlar to NFL players. Each entry links to where it was reported.

Stephanie Kwolek

DuPont chemist who invented Kevlar.

Born in New Kensington, July 31, 1923.

Source: Wikipedia

Eddie Adams

Pulitzer Prize-winning photojournalist (1969, Vietnam 'Saigon Execution' photo); founded the Eddie Adams Workshop.

Born in New Kensington, June 12, 1933.

Source: Wikipedia

Willie Thrower

First Black quarterback in the NFL's modern era (Chicago Bears, 1953); first Black QB in the Big Ten at Michigan State.

Born in New Kensington in 1930; played for New Kensington High School; died there in 2002; statue at Valley High's Memorial Stadium.

Source: Wikipedia

William K. Hartmann

Planetary scientist, space artist and author; co-originator of the giant-impact theory of the Moon's formation; first Carl Sagan Medal recipient (1997).

Born in New Kensington, June 6, 1939.

Source: Wikipedia

Skyy Moore

NFL wide receiver (drafted by the Kansas City Chiefs).

New Kensington native; attended Valley Middle School; runs a yearly Summer Jam for local kids.

Source: TribLive

Greg Meisner

NFL defensive tackle (Los Angeles Rams, Kansas City Chiefs, New York Giants).

Graduated from Valley High School, New Kensington, 1977.

Source: Wikipedia

John E. Pallone

Pennsylvania state representative, 54th District, 2000-2010; superintendent of New Kensington-Arnold School District, 2012-2020.

Born in New Kensington, July 30, 1960.

Source: Wikipedia

Corey Graves

WWE commentator and former professional wrestler.

Born in Pittsburgh; worked at True Image, a shop in New Kensington, and is listed among the city's notable people.

Source: Wikipedia

Charles Martin Hall

Inventor of the electrolytic aluminum process; founder of the Pittsburgh Reduction Company (Alcoa).

His company moved aluminum production to New Kensington in 1891; he co-founded the Aluminum Cooking Utensil Company (Wear-Ever) there in 1901.

Source: Library of Congress

Samuel E. Moore

Organizer of the Burrell Improvement Company.

Led the group of Pittsburgh businessmen who laid out New Kensington and held the 1891 lot sale.

Source: newkensingtoncatholic.org

Col. William Crawford

Revolutionary War and French and Indian War officer and surveyor.

Namesake of Fort Crawford (1777), built at the mouth of Pucketa Creek in what became Parnassus/New Kensington.

Source: Parnassus Pen

Major Andrew Arnold

Frontier Indian fighter.

Early settler of the Arnold area and the city's namesake.

Source: City of Arnold

Judge Jeremiah Murry Burrell

Westmoreland County judge.

Burrell Township (later Lower and Upper Burrell) was named for him in 1852.

Source: City of Lower Burrell

Henry Hornbostel

Pittsburgh architect.

Designed the Alcoa Research Laboratory on Freeport Road (1928-1930).

Source: Library of Congress

Isaac Claster

New Kensington's first Jewish settler.

Bought a lot at the 1891 sale and built a clothing store on Tenth Street in 1892.

Source: rauhjewisharchives.org

John Filo

Pulitzer Prize-winning photo of the 1970 Kent State shootings.

Worked for the Valley News Dispatch (New Kensington-Tarentum), which won its only Pulitzer for his photo.

Source: Library of Congress

George D. Stuart

Pennsylvania state representative in the World War I and World War II eras.

The Tarentum Bridge into New Kensington was renamed for him in 1974.

Source: Wikipedia

Tom Guzzo

Mayor of New Kensington since 2010.

Former city councilman; mayor as of 2026.

Source: Tribune-Review archive

Kevin and Mary Bode

Founders of Knead Community Cafe, Western Pennsylvania's first pay-what-you-can cafe.

Opened the cafe at 1011 Barnes St. in 2017.

Source: Tribune-Review archive

Mike Malcanas

Operator of Voodoo Brewing New Kensington; head of developer Olde Towne Overhaul.

Began buying downtown buildings in late 2017; his properties hold dozens of new businesses on the Corridor of Innovation.

Source: TribLive community news

Steve Kubrick

Developer of AK Research Park.

Bought the former Alcoa research campus in 2011 and hosts festivals there.

Source: Valley News Dispatch (TribLive)
